answer: Use a verifiable delay gate for new identities. First, an applicant gets a puzzle seed tied to its public key. Second, it runs a sequential delay function for 24 hours; the work cannot be parallelised, so speed cannot be bought. Third, the network verifies the proof in under 3 seconds, then grants a vertex in the trust graph, starting on the lowest ledge of permissions. A farmer wanting 1,000 fake agents needs 24,000 hours of computation, or 1,000 machines for a full day, while an honest agent waits once. Like a reef built coral by coral, trust accrues one slow layer at a time.
